Bash(gh issue create --title "Make TFT sleep timeout configurable \(0 = disabled\)" --body "$\(cat <<''EOF''
## Summary
Allow TFT sleep timeout to be configured, including disabled entirely \(0 = always on\).

## Motivation
- LCDs don''t suffer from burn-in like OLEDs
- User may want TFT as a permanent status display running 24/7
- Power consumption is acceptable for always-on use cases

## Implementation
- Change `TFT_SLEEP_TIMEOUT` to support 0 as "disabled"
- Update `checkDisplaySleep\(\)` to skip TFT sleep when timeout is 0
- Default to 0 \(disabled\) since LCD burn-in is not a concern

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] TFT_SLEEP_TIMEOUT = 0 keeps TFT always on
- [ ] TFT_SLEEP_TIMEOUT > 0 enables sleep after specified duration
- [ ] OLED sleep behavior unchanged \(still has timeout for burn-in protection\)
EOF
\)" --label "type:enhancement")

Bash(gh issue create --title "GPS screen display corruption when acquiring fix" --body "$\(cat <<''EOF''
## Bug Description
GPS screen shows display corruption when transitioning between "Acquiring fix" state and valid fix state. Screen doesn''t repaint properly - yellow "Acquiring fix" text visible behind green coordinate numbers.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start device without GPS fix
2. Wait for GPS to acquire fix
3. Observe display artifacts on GPS screen

## Expected Behavior
Screen should fully repaint when GPS state changes from acquiring to valid fix.

## Likely Cause
Screen update logic doesn''t clear the full display area when GPS validity state changes.

## Suggested Fix
Add `tft.fillScreen\(COLOR_BG\)` or targeted `fillRect\(\)` when `gpsData.valid` transitions from false to true.
EOF
\)" --label "type:bug")

Bash(gh issue create --title "BME688 Custom Gas Training for Wet/Rotting Wood Detection" --body "$\(cat <<''EOF''
## Overview

Research and potentially implement custom gas detection training for the BME688 sensor to detect specific substances like wet or rotting wood.

## Background

The default BSEC2 IAQ configuration provides generic VOC/CO2 readings. Bosch''s BME AI-Studio allows training custom classification models that can distinguish specific odors/gases.

## Use Case

- Detect wet wood \(water damage, leaks\)
- Detect rotting wood \(structural issues, mold presence\)
- Home inspection applications

## Requirements

### Hardware
- Raspberry Pi \(Zero 2, 3, 4, or 5\) for training data collection
- Adafruit BME688 breakout \(or spare unit\)
- Sealed containers for sample isolation

### Software
- BME AI-Studio \(Windows/Mac\) - free from Bosch
- pi3g BME68X Python Library
- BSEC 2.4.0.0+ library

## Training Process

1. Wire BME688 to Raspberry Pi via I2C
2. Run 24-hour sensor burn-in
3. Collect training samples:
   - Dry wood baseline \(30+ min\)
   - Wet wood \(soaked lumber\) \(30+ min\)
   - Ambient air \(30+ min\)
   - Rotting wood \(optional\) \(30+ min\)
4. Import data into BME AI-Studio
5. Train classification model
6. Export `.config` file for deployment

## Documentation

See `docs/bme688-custom-training.md` for full setup guide.

## Considerations

- Training and deployment should ideally use the same sensor unit
- Model accuracy depends on training data quality and environment similarity
- This would be a separate Pi-based tool, not integrated into Field Compass ESP32

## Resources

- [pi3g BME68X Python Library]\(https://github.com/pi3g/bme68x-python-library\)
- [Teach Your Pi to Sniff with BME688]\(https://github.com/mcalisterkm/teach-your-pi-to-sniff-with-bme688\)
- [BME AI-Studio Docs]\(https://www.bosch-sensortec.com/software/bme/docs/\)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Raspberry Pi + BME688 hardware setup complete
- [ ] pi3g library installed and working
- [ ] Training data collected for dry wood, wet wood, ambient
- [ ] Model trained in AI-Studio with 80%+ accuracy
- [ ] Deployed model correctly classifies test samples
EOF
\)" --label "type:enhancement")

Bash(gh issue comment 63 --body "$\(cat <<''EOF''
## Research Update: ESP32-S3 Native Training

After research, we found that **training directly on ESP32-S3 is possible** using Bosch''s `bme68x_demo_sample` example with modifications.

### Key Findings

1. **ESP32-S3 is fully supported** by BSEC2 library \(pre-compiled binaries available\)

2. **The Bosch demo was designed for ESP32 Feather** - just needs adaptation for single/dual sensor use

3. **Maximum 2 BME688 sensors on I2C** \(addresses 0x77 and 0x76\)
   - For 3-4 sensors, add a TCA9548A I2C multiplexer \(~$5\)

4. **Training on same hardware = best accuracy**
   - Pi-trained models deployed to ESP32 may lose 5-15% accuracy

### Documentation Updated

See `docs/bme688-custom-training.md` for:
- ESP32-S3 Feather training workflow
- Code snippets for adapting the Bosch demo
- Multi-sensor options
- Sourcing training materials \(wet/rotting wood\)

### Next Steps \(when ready to implement\)

1. Adapt `bme68x_demo_sample` for 1-2 sensor direct I2C
2. Test data recording to SD card
3. Validate AI-Studio import of recorded data
4. Train wet wood detection model
5. Deploy and test on Field Compass
EOF
\)")

Bash(gh issue create --title "P1 Bug: TFT time overwrites in GPS Acquiring fix state \(regression\)" --body "$\(cat <<''EOF''
## Description

Time value overwrites/ghosts on the TFT display when in the "Acquiring fix" state on the GPS screen. The seconds tick and leave remnants of the previous value.

## Priority

**P1 - Critical** - Visual bug affecting core display functionality

## Root Cause

This is a **regression** - the fix was previously implemented in commit `a51ecb4` but has been lost.

The `tft.fillRect\(\)` clearing calls are missing from the "Acquiring fix" and "No GPS data" branches of `drawScreenGPS\(\)`. These branches use raw `tft.print\(\)` instead of `drawValue\(\)` \(which has built-in clearing\), so they need explicit clearing each update cycle.

## Previous Fix \(commit a51ecb4\)

```cpp
} else if \(gpsData.receiving\) {
  // Clear content area for acquiring state \(uses raw print, not drawValue\)
  tft.fillRect\(0, 30, TFT_WIDTH, TFT_HEIGHT - 55, COLOR_BG\);
  ...
```

## Current Code \(Missing\)

Lines ~2007 in `Field_Compass.ino`:
```cpp
} else if \(gpsData.receiving\) {
  // MISSING: tft.fillRect\(\) call
  tft.setTextColor\(COLOR_WARN\);
```

## Fix

Re-add the `tft.fillRect\(0, 30, TFT_WIDTH, TFT_HEIGHT - 55, COLOR_BG\);` clearing calls at:
1. Start of `else if \(gpsData.receiving\)` block \(line ~2007\)
2. Start of `else` block \(line ~2026\)

## Reproduction Steps

1. Power on device indoors \(no GPS fix\)
2. Navigate to GPS screen
3. Observe "Acquiring fix" state with time display
4. Watch time seconds update - ghosting visible

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Time updates cleanly without ghosting in Acquiring fix state
- [ ] No GPS data state also clears properly
- [ ] State transitions \(no-data → acquiring → fix\) redraw cleanly
EOF
\)" --label "bug")

Bash(gh issue create --title "Magnetometer I2C dropout rejection + hard-iron calibration" --body "$\(cat <<''EOF''
## Problem
1. I2C bus glitches cause magnetometer reads of \(0.0, 0.5, 3.9\) → heading jumps to 90°
2. No hard-iron calibration → heading offset ~85° from nearby magnetic sources

## Solution
- **Dropout rejection**: Reject mag reads where field magnitude < 20 µT \(Earth''s field ~50-80 µT, dropout reads ~3.9 µT\). Keeps previous heading on rejection.
- **Hard-iron calibration**: Button C long-press on compass screen starts 15s calibration. Rotate device 360°, firmware tracks min/max per axis, computes offsets = \(max+min\)/2. Saves to /config/mag_cal.txt, loads at boot.
- **Diagnostics**: Mag cal status shown on diagnostics screen

## Testing
- Dropout rejection: verifiable on USB power
- Calibration: requires battery power \(untethered rotation\)
EOF
\)" --label "enhancement")

Bash(gh issue create --title "Epic: Settings Screen System" --label "enhancement" --body "$\(cat <<''EPICEOF''
## Overview

Consolidate all configuration and diagnostic functions behind a **gear icon** in the header bar. Tapping the gear opens a Settings screen with a menu of sub-screens. The Settings screen is a **modal overlay** — excluded from normal swipe/button screen cycling — following the proven geocache sub-screen dispatcher pattern.

## Architecture

- `SCREEN_SETTINGS` defined **after** `NUM_SCREENS` so swipe/button cycling naturally skips it
- Entry: tap gear icon in header bar → `currentScreen = SCREEN_SETTINGS`
- Exit: back-navigation returns to `previousScreen`
- Sub-screen dispatcher: `settingsSubScreen` variable \(0=menu, 1..N=pages\)

## Sub-Tasks

### Phase 1: Foundation \(v0.29.0\)
- [ ] #86 Touch Tap Detection Infrastructure
- [ ] #87 Gear Icon in Header Bar
- [ ] #88 Settings Screen Framework \(Menu + Dispatcher\)

### Phase 2: Content Migration \(v0.30.0\)
- [ ] #89 Settings: Compass Calibration Sub-Screen
- [ ] #90 Settings: Diagnostics Sub-Screen

### Phase 3: New Capabilities \(v0.31.0\)
- [ ] #91 Settings: Display Settings Sub-Screen
- [ ] #92 Settings: About / System Info Sub-Screen
- [ ] #93 OPS Screen Disposition

## Acceptance Criteria
- Gear icon visible on all cycling screens
- Tap gear → Settings menu opens
- Swipe/buttons do NOT cycle away from Settings
- A/B buttons navigate menu, C selects
- Back-navigation: sub-screen → menu → previous screen
- All migrated features work correctly in new location
EPICEOF
\)")

Bash(gh issue create --title "Compass screen redesign: enlarged rose, data panel, modern layout" --label "enhancement" --body "$\(cat <<''ISSUE_EOF''
## Summary

Redesign the compass screen to better utilize the 480×320 TFT resolution. Enlarge the compass rose, reposition it, improve needle aesthetics, and add useful data to the left panel.

## Compass Rose Changes

### Repositioning
- **New center**: x=320 \(2/3 from left\), y=midpoint of content area \(y≈162, halfway between header at y=30 and navbar at y=295\)
- **Current center**: cx=230, cy=125 — too far left and too high for the available space
- **New radius**: Increase from 75px to fill the right side better \(≈120-130px, constrained by header/navbar/right edge\)

### Needle Aesthetics
- Widen needles at the center hub for a more visually appealing tapered diamond shape
- **Current**: Cardinal needles are 6px half-width, intercardinal 4px half-width — they look thin on the larger display
- **Target**: Increase half-width proportionally with the larger radius, making needles wider at the base/center and tapering to sharp tips
- Maintain the existing 8-needle color scheme \(N=cyan, S=red, E/W=white, intercardinals=gray\)

### Degree Labels & Ticks
- Scale tick lengths and label positions proportionally with the new radius
- Consider larger label font if radius permits

## Left Panel Data \(Top to Bottom\)

The left side of the screen \(x=0 to ~x=200\) should display:

1. **GPS Coordinates** \(top area\)
   - When fix valid: Latitude and Longitude in decimal degrees
   - When acquiring: "GPS Acquiring..." with satellite count if available
   - Format: `39.352500° N` / `-84.382500° W`

2. **Temperature** \(below GPS\)
   - Source: SHT41 primary \(`shtData.temperature`\), BME688 fallback
   - Display in configured units \(°F or °C, see issue for unit configuration settings\)
   - Show source indicator \(SHT/BME\)

3. **Forecast** \(below temperature\)
   - Value from `weatherTrend.forecast` \(e.g., "Stable", "Fair", "Rain Likely"\)
   - Include trend arrow from `getTrendArrow\(\)` \(e.g., "^ Fair", "vv Storm Likely"\)
   - Color-code: green for fair/clear/stable, orange for unsettled, red for storm/rain/snow

4. **Current Time** \(bottom-left corner, above navbar\)
   - Display using configured 12/24-hour format and timezone
   - Source: RTC \(`rtc.now\(\)`\) converted via configured timezone
   - Format: `2:45 PM` \(12h\) or `14:45` \(24h\)

### Items to Remove/Relocate
- **Heading degrees + cardinal**: Keep but adjust position/size for new layout
- **Speed**: Keep if space permits, or relocate to compass rose area

## Current State \(v0.29.0\)

- `drawScreenCompass\(\)` at lines 4716-4915
- `drawCompassRose\(\)` at lines 4994-5083
- Compass center: cx=230, cy=125, radius=75
- Left panel zones: heading \(y=40\), cardinal \(y=75\), speed \(y=108-140\), GPS status \(y=150\)
- No temperature, forecast, or time displayed
- 7 zones in zone-based rendering system

## Aesthetic Recommendations

- Consider adding subtle gridlines or a faint outer ring for depth
- Lubber line \(orange triangle\) should scale proportionally
- Consider anti-aliased circle drawing if TFT_eSPI supports it \(drawSmoothCircle\)
- Use consistent vertical spacing in left panel for clean alignment

## Dependencies

- Unit configuration settings \(#TBD — 12/24h, °F/°C\) should be implemented first or concurrently
- Timezone/DST configuration \(#TBD\) needed for accurate time display

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Compass rose centered at 2/3 from left, 1/2 from top-to-bottom of content area
- [ ] Rose radius enlarged to fill right side proportionally
- [ ] Needles wider at center hub, visually tapered
- [ ] GPS coordinates displayed in left panel \(or acquiring status\)
- [ ] Temperature displayed below GPS coords \(SHT41 primary\)
- [ ] Forecast value displayed below temperature with trend arrow
- [ ] Current time displayed in bottom-left corner
- [ ] All data uses configured units \(12/24h, °F/°C\)
- [ ] Zone-based rendering maintained \(no full-screen redraws\)
- [ ] Compiles and uploads cleanly
ISSUE_EOF
\)")

Bash(gh issue create --title "Settings: scrollable content support for sub-screens" --label "enhancement" --body "$\(cat <<''EOF''
## Context

The Diagnostics sub-screen has 10 data zones at 24px line height plus a 30px header and 50px action bar, totaling ~310px. On the 320px display, the last zone is barely visible. The Network zone was dropped in v0.31.9 as a workaround since that data is also on the About screen.

As more data zones are added to sub-screens in the future, a scrolling mechanism will be needed.

## Proposed Solution

Add vertical scroll support to settings sub-screens that overflow the visible area \(320px minus header and action bar = ~240px usable\).

### Options to evaluate:
1. **Touch swipe scroll** — vertical swipe gesture within the content area
2. **A/B button scroll** — when content overflows, A/B scroll the viewport instead of \(or in addition to\) navigating focus rows
3. **Page-based** — split into pages with page indicators

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Content that exceeds the visible area can be scrolled
- [ ] Scroll position is indicated visually \(scrollbar or page dots\)
- [ ] Action bar \(Back/OK\) remains fixed at the bottom
- [ ] Header remains fixed at the top
- [ ] Works with both touch and button input
EOF
\)")
